# Web front end

## Scope

Applies when the change touches HTML, CSS, browser code. Not when the screen is a native mobile app, or the change is server-only. Neighbours: `aidd-team:accessible-ui`, `aidd-team:prototyping`, `aidd-team:product-defaults`.

## Dated obligations

| From | Obligation | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-09-11 | CRA reporting applies where the front end is part of a product with digital elements (`aidd-team:incident-response`), and the main obligations from 2027-12-11. A website that supports no product's function is out of scope (Recital 12). | S10 |
| 2026-12-09 | Beside the CRA, the EU Product Liability Directive (EU) 2024/2853: software placed on the market after this date is a product, and a missing update can make it defective. | S10 |

## Checklist by loop step

| Step | Item | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Before the first edit (`aidd gate --paths`) | Name the pages, components, and states the change touches; a user-facing change needs the product designer and `design.files`. A front end that is part of a product with digital elements is in CRA scope. A site that sells to EU consumers, or offers banking, e-books, or passenger transport, meets the European Accessibility Act, which builds on WCAG. | S1, S10 |
| Before the first edit (`aidd gate --paths`) | Product defaults (`dark_mode`, `responsive`, `i18n_ready`, `perf_budget`, `public_page_basics`, `legal_placeholders`, `transactional_email`, `security_headers`): build each one `project.defaults.disabled` does not name, as `aidd-team:product-defaults` says. | — |
| Specify | Acceptance names every state per screen (empty, loading, error, partial, success, offline) and the keyboard path through it. | S1 |
| Specify | The browser support target is Baseline Widely available (or a named Baseline year) in the Spec; a feature outside it has a fallback. | S6 |
| Specify | No non-essential cookie, storage, or tracker runs before consent where ePrivacy Art. 5(3) applies. A Global Privacy Control signal is an opt-out where a US state law requires it, as California, Colorado, Connecticut, Texas, and others do. | S8 |
| Specify | Rendering per route: static or server-rendered by default, client-rendered only for an app-like screen; the Spec names the JavaScript each route hydrates. Server data lives in one query cache with its staleness (`aidd-team:caching`), and UI state stays local or in the URL. | S9 |
| Implement | Semantic HTML first, ARIA only where HTML has no element; focus order and a visible focus ring preserved. | S1 |
| Implement | No inline script and no `unsafe-inline`: nonces or hashes under the CSP. Every third-party script is named in the Spec and pinned with `integrity` (SRI), or self-hosted when its bytes change by design. A `Permissions-Policy` turns off the features the page does not use. | S3, S7 |
| Implement | Session cookies are `Secure`, `HttpOnly`, and `SameSite=Lax` or `Strict`, with the `__Host-` prefix. A state-changing request checks a CSRF token or the `Origin` header. | S4 |
| Review | Untrusted strings reach the DOM only through escaping or a sanitizer, with Trusted Types enforced (`require-trusted-types-for 'script'`) where the engines support it; URLs are validated before `href` or `src`. | S4, S3 |
| Roll out | Core Web Vitals field data and the client error rate are the observe signals. | S2 |

## Test commands

| Command | Proves | How | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CSP evaluation | no `unsafe-inline` and no wildcard source in the policy | Google CSP Evaluator or a lint step in CI | S3 |
| ESLint accessibility and security rules | no accessibility or injection anti-pattern in the code | `eslint` with the accessibility rules for the team's `web-framework` (`eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y@6.10.2` on JSX, `eslint-plugin-vuejs-accessibility` on Vue templates) and `eslint-plugin-security@4.1.0`, in the test commands | S1, S4 |
| Design-token lint | no raw color, size, or space outside the repository's design tokens | `stylelint@17.15.0` with `color-no-hex` and the `stylelint-declaration-strict-value@1.12.1` plugin's `scale-unlimited/declaration-strict-value` on color properties; on JSX, ESLint `no-restricted-syntax` on a literal color in a `style` object | S5 |
| Browser support check | no API outside the Baseline target without a fallback | `eslint-plugin-compat` (7.0.2) with the browserslist query `baseline widely available` (browserslist 4.29.3), in the lint step | S6 |
| Cookie and tracker consent test | no non-essential cookie, storage, or third-party request before consent, and none after a refusal or a `Sec-GPC: 1` request | the team's `e2e-test` runner, by default `@playwright/test` (1.64.1), in a fresh context: record cookies, storage, and requests before and after each consent choice | S8 |

- From `aidd-team:accessible-ui`: Accessibility per state, Keyboard-only flows.
- From `aidd-team:prototyping`: Screenshot matrix.
- From `aidd-team:product-defaults`: Performance budget, Both themes, Responsive and targets, Security headers.

## Keep it current

Each entry is due after its `review_every_days` (else emerging 90 days, established 365) or by its `review_due`. An emerging one applies only when the change needs it, said in the Spec. One `aidd eval standards` lists as due is looked up in Specify, and a missing one is proposed to aidd's `schemas/industry-standards.json`.
